source_text: So, the work in progress section of your breakdown is confusing.  It includes a mix of READY and WAITING.  Neither of those statuses make immediate sense as me as a status for work in progress, since they sound  like "stuck" or "terminal" states.

reply_text:
㊥ (work in progress) Agreed: READY and WAITING describe rows nobody is working on, so they don't belong there. WORK IN PROGRESS now shows, for each row being worked on, who is on it and what they're doing. If the row also depends on a failing row that nobody has taken, it adds a "will also need" line. The READY, NEEDS A CHECK and BLOCKED sections now list only unassigned rows, so the two groups no longer overlap.

```
6. WORK IN PROGRESS (18)
  [codex-17] ▒ Array.append
        doing: fixing operand types lost in the generated-support `≤` expansion
  [codex-18] ▒ mkEOIError, FileMap.ofString (+loop), Array.back!
        doing: investigating a numeral given type TSyntax inside the list macro
        will also need (unassigned): ParserState.mkUnexpectedError   ← mkEOIError only
  [codex-19] ▓ InputContext.atEnd
        doing: fixing wrong results (Prop→Bool decide; Bind.bind binders)
  [codex-4]  ▒ Lean.Compiler.LCNF.mkDeclExt
        doing: fixing the next blocker (β: filterMap result type)
        will also need (unassigned): PersistentHashMap.foldl, PersistentHashMap.insertAux, instMonadEIO, instMonadEIO._aux_13
  [codex-6]  ▓ the 11 untested rows
        doing: writing and running their Lean checks
```

The full output, from `python3 /tmp/pyreg/overnight/rowtree.py`, lists each row on its own line.

㊟ (what "will also need" shows) Even when codex-4 clears `β`, `mkDeclExt` won't compile until four other failing rows do, and nobody is on those yet. Two of them are the instance-naming rows at the top of the ready list. So repairing instance naming would also unblock `mkDeclExt`.

㊢ (where the status comes from) The "doing" text lives in `rowstatus.json`. I update it each time I dispatch or close a job, so it's only as current as my last dispatch.
